name: Julie Lippert
fact: Lippert, a Paducah junior, was WKU homecoming queen for 1983, crowned at the Morehead game by the 1982 queen Mary Beth DeCastro; Lambda Chi Alpha and Alpha Gamma Rho sponsored her candidacy. She was Administrative Vice-President of Associated Student Government the following year.

name: Shiela Marie Waninger
fact: Waninger was president of the Phi Mu chapter at Western in 1982-83, the year before she sat in the Congress as alternate for the College of Education. The Talisman describes her as a junior from Fulda, Indiana, and quotes her on the chapter’s recruiting: the volume spells her first name Shelia.

name: Alan Jackson
kind: SEARCHED, NOT FOUND - no portrait exists in reach
fact: Alan Lawrence Jackson sat for no class portrait in any volume that could hold him, and the two photographs the archive does reach both hide his face. The 1980 Talisman index gives him exactly two pages, 'Jackson, Alan Lawrence 124, 423'. Printed p. 423 is a 'Student teacher' feature whose caption reads that helping kids with their social studies at McNeill Elementary School is part of sophomore Alan Jackson's contribution to tutoring efforts for his fraternity: the frame holds two elementary-school children facing the camera and one figure in the foreground with the back of the head to the lens, which is the tutor, so his face is not in the picture. Printed p. 124 is the Halloween spread, and its caption on p. 125 names five studio subjects, Molly and Betsy Bogdan, Alan Jackson, Candy Bush and Kathleen Hancock. He is the only man of the five and the p. 124 right-hand frame is the only man on the page, so the identification is sound, but the whole point of the frame is a Hallowe'en skull mask and makeup covering the face. The 1981 index lists him with no page numbers at all, so he is in no photograph in that volume. The 1982 index gives him one page, 'Jackson, Alan Lawrence 266', the Kappa Alpha Psi pledging feature 'Step in line' on pp. 266-267, where he is named twice in the body and once in a caption as the owner of the apartment the picture was taken in, and is in none of the four photographs. He was a senior that year, so the 1982 volume is his last chance at a grid cell and he is not in it. Corroboration that this is the right man and not a namesake: the 1980 caption calls him a Tampa, Fla., sophomore, the 1982 body text a Plant City, Fla., senior (two towns twenty miles apart in the same county, and the class years line up), and he is a Kappa Alpha Psi brother, which fits the Chair of Minority Affairs. Note that the 1982 caption on p. 266 calls him a Paducah senior, contradicting its own body text on the same page.

name: METHOD: archive.org 1986 and 1987 Talismans, corrected leaf arithmetic
kind: correction to a recorded offset - costs a wasted download if you get it wrong
fact: Two separate numbers, and the earlier notes conflated them. (1) PAGE IMAGES: printed page = image leaf minus 3, for BOTH 1986 and 1987. Verified against printed folios: 1987 image leaf n117 is p. 114 (the Associated Student Government spread), n365 is p. 362, n372 is p. 369, n374 is p. 371; 1986 image leaf n195 is p. 192, n373 is p. 370, n374 is p. 371, n378 is p. 375, n379 is p. 376. The same rule holds for 1980: image leaf n426 is p. 423 and n427 is p. 424. (2) OCR TEXT STREAM: the leaf number that scripts/talisman.py computes by bisecting the hOCR page index runs THREE HIGHER than the image leaf on the 1987 item. Stream leaf 120 is image leaf 117. So from a search hit, image leaf = stream leaf minus 3 and printed page = stream leaf minus 6. Fetching the page at the stream's own leaf number lands three pages late, which is what made the 1987 index look as though A ran to R.

name: Mark Chesnut
kind: SEARCHED, NOT FOUND - indexed twice, both times to a table of names
fact: He is in the archive's reach and still has no face. The 1980 and 1981 Talisman name indexes list every enrolled student and print page numbers only against the pages where a person actually appears, so his entries are exhaustive. 1980 index: 'Chesnut, Mark Cameron 257', one page. Printed p. 257 is the intramural champions table, where he is named twice, at Racquetball (D) as 'Mark Chesnut and Mitch Gum (Sigma Alpha Epsilon)' and at Tennis (D) as 'Mark Chesnut (Sigma Alpha Epsilon)'. The only photograph on the page is an uncaptioned water polo frame. 1981 index: 'Chesnut, Mark Cameron 234', one page. Printed p. 234 is the same table a year on, Badminton (s) 'Mark Chestnut (Sigma Alpha Epsilon)' and Racquetball (d) 'Mark Chestnut/Mitch Gum', with an uncaptioned flag football photograph below it. Neither is a picture of him. He sat for no class portrait in either volume. He is not in the 1981 Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter photograph on printed p. 314, whose caption names all thirty-eight members in five rows. And he is not in the 1982 volume at all: the only occurrences of the string in that book are Chestnut Street. The volumes print him both ways, Chesnut in the index and Chestnut in the 1981 table, and the 1980 text calls him 'a junior accounting major', which fits the man who was ASG Treasurer the following year.

name: John Holland
kind: FOUND IN THE BOOK, LOST TO A SCAN DEFECT - the page that should carry his portrait is blank
fact: This is the nearest miss on the block and it is worth someone's time if a second copy of the 1985 Talisman ever gets scanned. He is definitely in the volume: the index (PDF leaf 188) reads 'Holland, Cheryl 102 / Holland, Helen 32 / Holland, John M. 3??, 3??' with two page numbers in the three hundreds that the scan is too faded to resolve, then Hollenbeck, Frank 119. The volume also names him in the text: printed pp. 202-203, the ASG book exchange feature 'Bucks for books', quotes 'John Holland, a Louisville senior and committee co-chairman' and again at the end, and that spread's only photographs are a still life of books and an uncaptioned woman reading The Book Exchanger, so it gives no face. THE DEFECT: the 1985 juniors portrait grid runs 320 (Cou-Dye), 321 (Eans-Gal), then jumps to 325 (Hoo-McC), with 323 and 324 a feature spread carrying no grid. The missing run Gal to Hoo, which is exactly where HOLLAND falls, is printed page 322 - and printed page 322 is COMPLETELY BLANK in the TopSCHOLAR scan (PDF leaf 163, left half of the spread, white from edge to edge). The index independently proves that page had content: it sends 'Hollinsworth, John A.' to 322. So his class portrait exists in the printed book and does not exist in the only digitisation the archive can reach. He is separately absent from the 1985 SENIORS grid, printed p. 301 (Seniors/Gri-Hou), whose H run goes Hofsass, Hogue, Holliday, Holman with no Holland, even though the book's own text calls him a senior; the Talisman evidently classed him a junior. And he is absent altogether from the 1984 volume - see the separate 1983-84 note.

name: SOURCE: the 1982 Talisman Associated Student Government group photograph, printed p. 241
kind: roster found, photograph unusable - read this before re-opening the 1981-82 officers
fact: This frame had never been worked on this block and it names FOUR of the fifteen officers, which is why it is written up in full even though nothing could be cut from it. THE CAPTION, read off the page image: 'ASSOCIATED STUDENT GOVERNMENT - Front row: Marcel Bush, Susan Albert, Kerrie Stewart, Lonnie Sears, Maurie McGarvey, Wennifer Knowles. Second row: Helen Crisp, Melinda Wood, Jeffrey Sharp, James Brumfield, Jeffrey Ice, Cristy Sisk, Becky Johnson. Third row: Laura Simms, David Will, Thomas Farmer, Melody Murphy, Maura Fleenor, John Holland, Susan Day, Douglas Ball. Back row: Mark Smith, Douglas Hoots, Alesia Canafax, Jeffrey Chapman, William Chandler, Jamie Nichols, Carol Gibson, Bridget Wyatt, James Whalen.' Six, seven, eight and nine: thirty people. WHY NOTHING WAS CUT: the TopSCHOLAR scan of the 1982 volume is 816 by 1123 pixels to a printed page, and this photograph occupies 371 by 213 of them for thirty people, so a face is twelve to eighteen pixels across - a quarter of the forty to sixty that the earlier note already calls unusable - and the group sits on tiered theatre seating with the four bands interleaved, so even the row a given head belongs to cannot be settled. Do not spend another run trying. WHAT IT IS WORTH ANYWAY: it puts Melody Murphy, John Holland, Douglas Ball and Mark Smith in ASG in 1981-82 on the organisation's own page, and John Holland's first office in the archive is 1983-84, so this is two years earlier than the record has him. It also independently confirms Susan Day, Jamie Nichols, Bridget Wyatt, James Brumfield and Maura Fleenor, all of whom already have faces from elsewhere in these volumes. The spread is PDF leaf 244 of dlsc_ua_records/405; printed page = leaf minus 3.

name: Doug Ball
kind: SEARCHED, NOT FOUND - three appearances, none of them a usable face
fact: The 1982 Talisman index gives 'Ball, Douglas Clair 109, 240, 263', three pages, and all three were opened. Printed p. 109 is the history-costumes feature 'Face to face', which quotes 'Doug Ball, a Louisville junior and portrayer of Gandhi' and 'Ball, a speech major', and whose only photograph is of Judy Carnes as Catherine the Great. Printed p. 240-241 is the Associated Student Government spread, where the group photograph's caption puts him eighth and last in the third row - unusable, see the source note on that frame. Printed p. 263 is the Greek section, which quotes 'Louisville junior Doug Ball' on the Pi Kappa Alpha parties; the Pi Kappa Alpha chapter photograph is on that page and its caption names all thirty-two members in four rows and he is not among them. He sat for no class portrait in 1982. He is in the 1980 and 1981 name indexes as 'Ball, Douglas Clair' with NO page numbers against him in either, which in those two volumes means enrolled but in no photograph. He is not in the 1983 volume's Associated Student Government photograph, p. 232, which names thirty-one members - consistent with the officer record, which has him resigning his 1982-83 Representative-at-Large seat. Also in the 1982 volume, and not him: Kim Ball, a Worthville senior, pp. 270 and 344.

name: BLOCK n8087 CLOSED - all fifteen officers accounted for
fact: Every one of the fifteen officers on _officers-n8087.json has now either a face or a written reason, and each name has its own note above giving the volumes opened and the exact alphabetical position read. FACES CUT, four: Stephen Kiehn (1984 Talisman p. 290, Delta Tau Delta, front row 1), Todd Duncan (1984 p. 299, Pi Kappa Alpha, back row 7), Pat Franke (1985 p. 273, Kappa Sigma, front row 6, and note the volume spells him Francke), and Debbie Thomas (1981 p. 356 junior grid), that last one flagged FACE PROVED PERSON NOT PROVED because two Deborah Thomases were enrolled and both were photographed. NOT FOUND, with reasons: Alan Jackson (two frames, one a Hallowe'en skull mask, one showing only the back of his head), Mark Chesnut (indexed twice, both to intramural results tables), Doug Ball, Melody Murphy and Mark Smith (all three only in the 1982 Associated Student Government group photograph, which is unusable at twelve pixels a face), John Holland (absent from the 1984 volume; his 1985 class portrait is on printed p. 322, which is BLANK in the only scan), Kim Robertson and Connie Hoffmann (absent from the index of the volume covering their year), Chris Millay and Dwight Austin (absent from the indexes of all three volumes that could hold them, 1986, 1987 and 1988, checked on the page images). Kelly S. Smith is a candidate not cut: the 1984 index's only Kelly Smith is Kelly ANNETTE and the officer list reads Kelly S. WHAT IS LEFT, and it is thin: nothing in the Talisman run 1980-1988 has been left unread for these fifteen. The only routes that could still produce a face are a College Heights Herald photograph from the right week, a second scan of the 1985 volume that has printed p. 322, or a source giving Kelly S. Smith or Mark Smith a middle name. Two general warnings for whoever comes next: the 1982-1985 volumes have no readable embedded text layer for index work and every negative here was read off the page images, and the 1984 Talisman has NO Associated Student Government group photograph or member roster at all, which is why the 1983-84 cohort is so hard.
